# Prompt Override — Reference Mode (Single Chunk)

Use this when **Mode = Reference (Omni)**, the render is a single chunk (Total Duration ≤ Chunk Size, no auto-split), and **Prompt Override** is switched ON with this text wired into the **Prompt Override** socket.

Reference images/audio still come from the **Characters / Location / Ref Video / Ref Audio** sections as normal — this only replaces the *prompt text* the Director would otherwise compile from those + the Timeline.

## Template

    subject_definitions:
    <Subject 1> is [character 1's identity — face, hair, clothing, distinguishing features] (from `<Picture 1>`).
    <Subject N> is [location/setting description, if a Location slot is filled] (from `<Picture N>`).

    summary:
    [reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1>[, <Subject 2>][ and <Subject N>].

    retention_analysis:
    <Subject 1> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture 1>`.
    <Subject N> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture N>`.

    detailed_description:
    [One style sentence — overall look, cinematography, performance style.]
    [Shot 1] [Action and dialogue, tagging every character as <Subject N> — never "REF N", that label only exists inside the Timeline UI.]

    overall_soundscape:
    [Real ambience description, OR N/A if this chunk's audio is a full song/music-video master being copied wholesale.]

    non_diegetic_music:
    [Same choice as overall_soundscape — real description, or N/A.]

## Tag numbering — don't guess this

- Every **filled** Ref Character slot gets one `<Subject N>`, in slot order, **skipping empty slots** — dense numbering, not fixed to the slot's own number.
- A filled **Location** slot gets the *next* `<Subject N>` after every character — always last, never before a character.
- `<Picture N>` numbering always matches its `<Subject N>`'s number, 1:1.

## Retention line format

Keep it terse — no re-description here, that only lives in `subject_definitions`:

    <Subject N> (presence): retention - matches `<Picture N>`.

- `(present throughout)` — only if that character/location appears in *every* shot of this chunk.
- `(appears in [Shot 2], [Shot 3])` — if it only enters partway through.

# Prompt Override — Reference Mode (Multiple Chunks)

Use this when **Mode = Reference (Omni)**, **Total Duration** is longer than **Chunk Size** (so the render auto-splits into 2+ chunks), and **Prompt Override** is switched ON.

One `Prompt Override` socket now carries text for **every** chunk at once — split it into sections with a header line, one per chunk:

    --- Chunk 1/2 ---
    [chunk 1's full template]

    --- Chunk 2/2 ---
    [chunk 2's full template]

Each chunk only ever receives its own section. No headers at all = the whole string is used unchanged for every chunk (old behavior — still exactly right for single-chunk renders, see the other note).

## Chunk 1 — identical to the single-chunk template

    --- Chunk 1/2 ---
    subject_definitions:
    <Subject 1> is [character 1's identity] (from `<Picture 1>`).
    <Subject N> is [location, if filled] (from `<Picture N>`).

    summary:
    [reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1>[ and <Subject N>].

    retention_analysis:
    <Subject 1> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture 1>`.
    <Subject N> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture N>`.

    detailed_description:
    [Style sentence.]
    [Shot 1] [Action/dialogue, tagging characters as <Subject N>.]

    overall_soundscape:
    [Real content, or N/A — see "Is it a music video?" on the single-chunk note.]

    non_diegetic_music:
    [Same choice.]

## Chunk 2+ — continuation

**Important:** the `<Video N>` continuity tag is currently OFF in the Director's own code (a deliberate active test) — visual continuity carries through the wired images alone. Don't add a `<Video N>` line by hand, it won't do anything extra.

Audio DOES still carry a tag — but only if the previous chunk generated its own score (i.e. **not** a Lip Sync/fully_copy chunk, which is already its own complete audio track with nothing to add on top):

    --- Chunk 2/2 ---
    subject_definitions:
    <Subject 1> is [character 1's identity] (from `<Picture 1>`).
    <Subject N> is [location, if filled] (from `<Picture N>`).
    <Audio M> is the tail end of the previous shot's own score/ambience.

    summary:
    [reference generation + audio reuse] The target video shows <Subject 1>[ and <Subject N>], carrying <Audio M> forward.

    retention_analysis:
    <Subject 1> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture 1>`.
    <Subject N> (present throughout): fully_preserved - matches `<Picture N>`.
    <Audio M> (previous shot's tail): partially_copy - the tail end of the previous shot's own score/ambience continues into this one.

    detailed_description:
    [Style sentence — repeat near-identically from Chunk 1.]
    [Shot 1] [Action/dialogue continuing directly from where Chunk 1 left off — no restart.]

    overall_soundscape:
    [Real content describing the carried ambience continuing, or N/A if a full-song master.]

    non_diegetic_music:
    [Same choice.]

If this chunk's audio actually IS a Lip Sync/fully_copy master, drop the `<Audio M>` lines and the `+ audio reuse` bracket bit entirely — the Director injects its own continuation instruction into this text automatically regardless of what you write here.

## More than 2 chunks?

Add more `--- Chunk N/M ---` sections the same way — 3, 4, however many. Any chunk beyond the last one you actually wrote reuses that last section's text automatically (with a warning in the ComfyUI console), rather than erroring.

integrated_multimodal_description:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, `<Picture 1>` (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

A sharp, dissonant string stab hits on the alarm's first flash, settling into a driving, anxious low pulse.

# Prompt Override — First/Last Frame Mode (Single Chunk)

Use this when **Mode = First/Last Frame**, the render is a single chunk, and **Prompt Override** is switched ON.

This mode has **no `<Subject N>` system at all** — only `<Picture N>` for whichever keyframe(s) are actually wired into Ref 1 (first frame) / Ref 2 (last frame), and only 3 sections instead of 6.

Use exactly ONE of the three opening lines below, matching what's actually wired — never invent a keyframe that isn't there.

## Both first AND last frame wired

    integrated_multimodal_description:
    How the reference pictures align with the target video — `<Picture 1>` (from [Shot 1]) aligns with the 0.00-second mark; `<Picture 2>` (from [Shot N — this chunk's last shot]) aligns with the MM:SS.mmm mark (this chunk's own end timestamp).
    [Style sentence.]
    [Shot 1] [Opening action, starting from <Picture 1>'s state.]
    [Shot N] [Closing action, converging on <Picture 2>'s state by chunk's end.]

    overall_soundscape:
    [Real content, or N/A — see "Is it a music video?" below.]

    non_diegetic_music:
    [Same choice.]

## First frame only

Opening line:

    For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, `<Picture 1>` (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

Then develop new action forward from it — don't just repeat/loop what's already visible in the image.

## Last frame only

Opening line:

    How the reference pictures align with the target video — `<Picture 1>` (from [Shot N — this chunk's last shot]) aligns with the MM:SS.mmm mark (this chunk's own end timestamp).

Infer a plausible earlier state and develop forward, converging on it by the chunk's end.

## `<Picture N>` numbering

`<Picture 1>` is ALWAYS the first frame, if one exists — even in a "last frame only" render, the last frame is still `<Picture 1>`, never `<Picture 2>`, because there's no first frame consuming that number.

# Muse Minimax Director

## Mode
- **Reference (Omni)** — multi-character/video/audio references, soft-followed
- **First/Last Frame** — Ref 1 = first frame, Ref 2 = last frame, locked exactly

## Generation
- **Total Duration** — the finished length
- **Chunk Size** — length of each single MiniMax call (auto-splits above ~15s)

## Resolution
- **Aspect Ratio / Megapixels** — output size
- **Multiple Of** — leave alone unless you know why you're changing it

## Sampling
- Standard sampler controls
- **Shift (video) / Shift (audio)** — advanced, leave at default

## Reference Settings
- **Ref Image Size** — "match" is faster, "max" is stronger identity but slower
- **Dialogue Language** — feeds every spoken line
- **Hybrid Continuation** — multi-chunk only, needs a First/Last-Frame model wired in

## Overall Style
One or two sentences setting the look of the whole clip — lighting, palette, camera feel.

## Soundscape & Music
- **Overall Soundscape** — ambience/physical sound
- **Non-Diegetic Music** — background score only the audience hears
- Blank or `N/A` if not needed

## Characters / Location
- Drop an image into **Ref 1–9** for each character, **Location** for the setting
- Type a description or click **Analyze**
- **Retention** — how strictly it's followed; leave on `fully preserved` unless intentionally blending

## Ref Video
*(optional)*
- **Subject description** — blank = pure motion/camera reference; fill in if a person/thing should be reused
- **Role** — Reference / Editing source / Continuation source
- **Include this clip's audio** — also pulls its sound in as a voice reference

## Ref Audio
*(optional)*
- A short voice sample + whose voice it is
- **Retention** — `reference` clones the voice/style; `fully copy` reuses the actual audio

## Timeline / CUTs
- One CUT per beat — drag block edges to change pacing
- Put `"quoted text"` in a CUT for dialogue — a **Speaker** dropdown appears

## Referring to things in CUT text

# Download These First — Custom Nodes

ComfyUI's own "Install Missing Custom Nodes" **will not catch any of these**. They're all called internally by other nodes' own code, not wired in as their own visible boxes on the canvas — so nothing flags them as missing. You only find out when a render fails partway through with an error. Install these before you try to run anything.

## Required

1. **[ComfyUI-H3-Multishot](https://github.com/jlucasmcrell/ComfyUI-H3-Multishot)** — needed for Two-Stage Sampling (on by default) and for every model/clip load the Muse Unified Loader does.
2. **[ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef](https://github.com/seitanism/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef)** — needed for VAE Re-encode Carry and Raw Latent Carry (both on by default). This is a fork — install this exact repo, not the original it's forked from.
3. **[ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)** — needed for SageAttention support in the Muse Unified Loader (on by default).

Restart ComfyUI after installing all three.

## Optional — only if you turn on the feature that needs them

4. **[ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF)** — only if you're using the Low VRAM or Balanced quality profile (the GGUF model route).
5. **[ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton)** — only if you switch on Sol-Attn in the Muse Unified Loader (off by default).

Once these are installed and ComfyUI has been restarted, you're ready to go — model downloads are covered separately in the Setup note.

widgets_values:
# Muse Minimax Director

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds per single generation call.

**Muse Minimax Director** is a timeline-based director node that sits on top of the stock `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. Instead of manually writing `<Picture N>` / `<Video N>` / `<Audio N>` tags into a single prompt box, you build a script visually:

- Drop up to 9 character images into **Ref 1-9** and a **Location** image, write a description for each (or click **Analyze**)
- Write your script as a sequence of **CUTs** along the timeline, and tick who's speaking on each one
- Optionally add reference video and reference audio — Ref Audio N automatically becomes Ref N's voice

It compiles all of that into MiniMax H3's own official prompt format, with every tag numbered exactly the way H3 itself assigns them, and long scripts automatically split into multiple chunks if they exceed a single ~15 second generation call. Check the node's `compiled_prompt` output any time you want to see exactly what was sent to H3.

## ⚠️ Required custom nodes — install these BEFORE you run anything

**ComfyUI's own "Install Missing Custom Nodes" will NOT catch any of these.** They're used internally by other nodes' own code, not as separate nodes on the canvas, so nothing will flag them as missing — you'll only find out when a render fails partway through with an error. Install all of these now:

- **[ComfyUI-H3-Multishot](https://github.com/jlucasmcrell/ComfyUI-H3-Multishot)** — required whenever Two-Stage Sampling runs, which is **on by default**. Also required unconditionally by the Muse Unified Loader for every single model/clip load.
- **[ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef](https://github.com/seitanism/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef)** — required whenever VAE Re-encode Carry or Raw Latent Carry run, which are **both on by default**. (This is a fork of [NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context](https://github.com/NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context) — install the fork, not the original.)
- **[ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)** — required by the Muse Unified Loader for SageAttention support, which is **on by default**.

Optional:

- **[ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF)** — only if you're using the lower-VRAM GGUF route (Low VRAM / Balanced quality profiles).

# Muse Minimax Director

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds per single generation call.

**Muse Minimax Director** is a timeline-based director node that sits on top of the stock `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. Instead of manually writing `<Picture N>` / `<Video N>` / `<Audio N>` tags into a single prompt box, you build a script visually:

- Drop up to 9 character images into **Ref 1-9** and a **Location** image, write a description for each (or click **Analyze**)
- Write your script as a sequence of **CUTs** along the timeline, and tick who's speaking on each one
- Optionally add reference video and reference audio — Ref Audio N automatically becomes Ref N's voice

It compiles all of that into MiniMax H3's own official prompt format, with every tag numbered exactly the way H3 itself assigns them, and long scripts automatically split into multiple chunks if they exceed a single ~15 second generation call. Check the node's `compiled_prompt` output any time you want to see exactly what was sent to H3.

## ⚠️ Required custom nodes — install these BEFORE you run anything

**ComfyUI's own "Install Missing Custom Nodes" will NOT catch any of these.** They're used internally by other nodes' own code, not as separate nodes on the canvas, so nothing will flag them as missing — you'll only find out when a render fails partway through with an error. Install all of these now:

- **[ComfyUI-H3-Multishot](https://github.com/jlucasmcrell/ComfyUI-H3-Multishot)** — required whenever Two-Stage Sampling runs, which is **on by default**. Also required unconditionally by the Muse Unified Loader for every single model/clip load.
- **[ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef](https://github.com/seitanism/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context-MultiRef)** — required whenever VAE Re-encode Carry or Raw Latent Carry run, which are **both on by default**. (This is a fork of [NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context](https://github.com/NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context) — install the fork, not the original.)
- **[ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)** — required by the Muse Unified Loader for SageAttention support, which is **on by default**.

Optional:

- **[ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF)** — only if you're using the lower-VRAM GGUF route (Low VRAM / Balanced quality profiles).
